anti_overlap: fd-llm-judge-reliability covers prompt design and rubric ambiguity in the eval scoring module
fd-dimension-construct-validity covers whether individual dimensions are psychometrically valid
fd-concurrency-reliability covers data loss during matrix execution
fd-reference-relative-scoring covers the paradigm choice of reference-relative evaluation
decision_lens: Prioritizes bias sources that systematically favor one model family in ways that are invisible from aggregate scores. A model that self-scores at 4.8/5 while peers score it at 3.2 is not a better model — it is a biased evaluator, and using it to select the production pipeline is a catastrophic mistake.
focus: Evaluator self-preference bias, ceiling effects, and statistical power in the N×M evaluator matrix
name: fd-eval-self-bias-ceiling
persona: An ML evaluation researcher specializing in LLM-as-judge methodology, with experience studying self-preference bias (models scoring their own outputs higher) and ceiling effects in benchmarks. Has published on positional bias and reference-free evaluation for NLG tasks.
review_areas: Examine whether the evaluator matrix test design computes self-evaluation cells (evaluator=reconstructor) separately and flags them as suspect in the output report
Check whether the calibration examples in DEFAULT_CALIBRATION are injected into every evaluator call or only some — calibration drift between runs means matrix cells are not on the same scale
Assess whether the 1-5 scale produces ceiling effects for the best models (>50% of scores at 5), which would collapse discrimination between top performers
Review whether the human-editor calibration ceiling row is scored by ALL evaluator models or a subset — if only some evaluators score it, cross-evaluator normalization is impossible

Examine whether the eval prompt includes the reconstruction model's identity (even implicitly via model artifacts in output), which could trigger self-preference bias in autoregressive models that recognize their own output style
Check whether inter-rater agreement (Spearman/Kendall) is computed across evaluators per dimension and whether any dimension has near-zero inter-rater agreement (rendering it useless as a signal)

severity_examples.condition: The matrix does not exclude or flag diagonal (self-evaluation) cells in aggregate rankings
severity_examples.scenario: A model consistently scores its own reconstructions 0.8 points higher than peers score the same reconstructions, but self-evaluation cells are included in the aggregate leaderboard, causing that model to appear best-in-class when it is mid-tier

severity_examples.condition: DEFAULT_CALIBRATION is not uniformly included in the eval prompt
severity_examples.scenario: Calibration examples are only injected when the --calibrate flag is passed, so production matrix runs and calibration runs are on different scoring scales, making cross-run comparison meaningless

severity_examples.condition: No check that human-editor row is complete before reporting normalized scores
severity_examples.scenario: The human-editor row is only scored by 3 of 9 evaluators because the run was interrupted, so the calibration ceiling cannot normalize the 6 remaining evaluators, invalidating cross-evaluator comparison

success_hints: A rigorous matrix report identifies self-eval cells separately, computes inter-rater Spearman per dimension, excludes diagonal cells from leaderboard aggregates, and refuses to report rankings when human-editor ceiling coverage is below 100%.
task_context: cipher_evaluator_matrix.py runs an N×M matrix of reconstruction models × evaluator models to identify the pareto-optimal LLM judge. The human-editor row serves as a calibration ceiling. The matrix is used to select which model evaluates the production CIPHER benchmark. After migrating to 1-5 scale (v2, 2026-03-28), ceiling effects and scoring distribution deserve fresh scrutiny.
